title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a smooth, projective, connected curve over F_p, with function field K. Let y = Spec K be the generic point and i : y -> X its inclusion. E_y is a constructible Q_ell-sheaf on y, which amounts to a continuous ell-adic representation of Gal(K^sep/K).

Aim: attach to E_y an L-function intrinsic to K. Grothendieck remarks this is reasonable because K determines X: X is the unique smooth projective model of K.

Definition: L*_{E_y}(t) := L(X, i_*E_y, t). Here i_* is the underived direct image. Its stalk at a closed point x is the inertia invariants E_y^{I_x}. So L* is Artin's (Weil's) L-function of the Galois representation, \prod_x det(1 - F_x t^{deg x} | E^{I_x})^{-1}.

Key input, Verdier duality on a curve: D(i_*E_y) = i_*(\check E_y)(1), up to the shift [2], which is irrelevant for L-functions. This is the statement that the 'middle extension' commutes with duality.

Grothendieck's functional equation for constructible sheaves on X (Lefschetz formula plus Poincare duality) is L(D F, 1/(pt)) = (-t)^{chi(F)} delta(F) L(F, t), with delta(F) a determinant of Frobenius on cohomology (the epsilon factor). Applied to F = i_*E_y, with chi*(E_y) := chi(i_*E_y) and delta*(E_y) := delta(i_*E_y), this gives:

L*_{\check E_y}(1/(pt)) = (-t)^{chi*} delta* L*_{E_y}(t).

Autodual case: suppose \check E_y = E_y(rho), for example rho = 1 for H^1 of an elliptic curve. A Tate twist rescales the variable, L*_{E(rho)}(t) = L*_E(p^{-rho} t), and leaves chi unchanged. So the equation becomes the boxed formula

L*_{E_y}(1/(qt)) = (-t)^{chi*(E_y)} delta*(E_y) L*_{E_y}(t), with q = p^{1+rho}.

This is the shape s <-> (1+rho) - s of the classical functional equation, e.g. for L-functions of elliptic curves over function fields. The page serves the program of cote 60: deducing functional equations of L-functions of Galois representations of global function fields from the cohomological (sheaf-theoretic) functional equation.

The neighbouring pages are unrelated Bourbaki 'Algèbre commutative' exercise drafts (determinantal ideals, lattices) on the reverse/other sheets.
errors: D(i_*E_y) = i_*(\check E_y)(1) omits the shift [2]; this is harmless for L-functions but strictly needed.
i_* must be the underived direct image (middle extension, i.e. inertia invariants). R i_* has nonzero R^1 at closed points, so the notation is ambiguous but evidently means i_*.

In the first displayed equation chi*(\check E_y) appears in the exponent, while the definition is given for E_y. The two agree in the self-dual case, and chi(i_*\check E) = chi(i_*E) in general by duality.
The sign/normalization of the twist (whether geometric Frobenius acts on Q_ell(1) by p^{-1}) is implicit. With that convention q = p^{1+rho} is correct.
The field is written F_p, though everything works over F_q.

ideas.what: L-function of an ell-adic Galois representation of a global function field defined as the L-function of the sheaf j_*E on the complete curve
ideas.modern_name: Artin/Weil L-function of a Galois representation via middle extension j_*
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Bourbaki 279, 1964); Weil (Dirichlet series and automorphic forms, 1971); Deligne (constantes des équations fonctionnelles, 1973)
ideas.where_published: Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 279 (1964), 'Formule de Lefschetz et rationalité des fonctions L'; SGA 5

ideas.what: Verdier duality commutes with j_* on a curve: D(j_*E) = j_*(E^vee)(1)[2]
ideas.modern_name: self-duality of middle extension (intermediate extension on curves)

ideas.what: Functional equation L(1/(qt)) = (-t)^chi delta L(t) for self-dual-up-to-twist representations, with q = p^{1+rho}
ideas.modern_name: functional equation of L-functions of (pure, self-dual) Galois representations over function fields; global epsilon factor = det(-Frob | H^*)

deep.surprise_reason: A clean working-out of a standard consequence of Grothendieck's own published functional equation (Bourbaki 279/SGA 5) for j_* of a Galois representation. Nothing new to specialists.
